analysis:
The only changed file is CHANGELOG.md, and the supplied patch changes only head lines 11-25. That hunk renames the v0.10.2 candidate heading to v0.10.3 and adds release notes about an M5 crash in the Gemma 4 and Qwen attention kernel. The notes also describe submodule bumps for libs/mlx-swift and libs/mlx (a re-pin to corrected MLX), and a KV-backend guard that binds to the tripped version. The two supplied units (head lines 1462-1872) are older changelog history and are not in the changed ranges, so they add no new behavior. Documentation changes do not alter any security control.

Threat models examined: T-041 (prefix-cache/SSD tier) is touched only in prose, because the changelog mentions the KV-backend guard and the contiguous fallback. Nothing in the supplied evidence changes the SSD cache TTL, HMAC lookup tags, crypto or scope. TB-003, TB-009, TB-011 and the attestation and App Attest threats are not affected by the visible text.

Unverified items for later review: the actual pin changes for libs/mlx-swift (eedca444 to 4926d3d9) and libs/mlx (ff4bb35b to 31f550af) are described but not shown as diffs. The changelog says the MLX 31f550af only corrects the kernel's arguments, which I cannot verify from the supplied evidence. If the submodule bump is in the PR, its contents (third-party MLX code running in the provider process that handles decrypted prompts, A-001/TB-007) merit separate supply-chain review. The statement that the guard clears on a version change is a behavior claim I cannot verify. No finding is raised, since the supplied evidence shows no concrete security regression.
